findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex now writes b.cache at the end of a potentially long concurrent build. Concurrent map iteration and map write can cause Go's fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic. This can be reached when searchSupport.init starts its watch goroutine before logging TotalDocs and a watch/search request lazily builds another index. TotalDocs should hold cacheMu.RLock for the iteration.

findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key are no longer serialized or deduplicated
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for its whole duration; now it only locks when inserting the finished index and never re-checks whether the same NamespacedResource was built concurrently. Two concurrent Search/handleEvent calls through getOrCreateIndex can both miss GetIndex and build the same key: for file-backed indexes both use the same directory path, so one can fail on the already-open index, and for memory indexes one finished index is overwritten in the cache and leaked without Close. Add per-key/single-flight building or a double-checked cache lookup under an appropriate lock.

findings.title: searchSupport.init has unsynchronized writes from errgroup workers
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, every errgroup worker executes totalBatchesIndexed++ and assigns to the shared outer err variable (line 190). These concurrent unsynchronized writes are a data race, can lose counter increments for the span attribute, and make the shared err value racy/redundant because errgroup already collects worker return values. Use an atomic counter and a local error variable inside each worker.

findings.title: NewResourceServer performs blocking index builds with an uncancellable background context
findings.body: NewResourceServer now synchronously calls s.Init(ctx), but ctx is derived internally from context.Background and is only cancelled by server.Stop, which cannot be called until the constructor returns. A slow or hung GetResourceStats/ListIterator index build therefore blocks construction indefinitely with no caller-supplied startup context or timeout, and a search-index failure now prevents creation of the whole resource server including non-search operations. Pass a caller context/timeout into construction or otherwise make eager initialization cancellable.

findings.title: Constructor does not clean up partial initialization on Init failure
findings.body: When s.Init fails in NewResourceServer, the function returns nil, err without calling s.cancel or lifecycle Stop. Init may already have started side effects, notably searchSupport.init's background-context watch goroutine or a partially started watcher, but the discarded server gives the caller no handle to stop them. This leaks goroutines/pollers that continue consuming storage events after construction has failed; clean up the server context and started components on the error path.

findings.title: Postgres storage-server integration coverage is disabled instead of fixed
findings.body: The change adds an unconditional postgres skip to TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer just as the PR changes storage-server startup to eagerly initialize unified storage. That removes CI coverage for the eager Init/SQL path on one supported database backend, so a postgres-specific startup regression would not be caught. Fix the underlying postgres failure or keep the skip tied to a tracked, narrowly scoped condition.
